issues.legal_issue: A later validation provision does not reopen a transfer whose invalidity had already been finally adjudicated before that provision came into force.
material_facts: The transfer was made before the later validation provision came into force.
In proceedings concerning the transfer, the Collector found it invalid, and that finding was upheld through the subsequent proceedings before the Revenue Tribunal and High Court.
After those proceedings had concluded, the transferee applied to have the same transfer validated under the later provision.
issues.conclusion: The later validation provision did not apply to undo the completed adjudication, and the Mamlatdar had no jurisdiction to issue a certificate validating the transfer.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 63 and 64 of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 rendered certain transfers invalid. Under section 84, the Collector could determine whether a transfer contravened those provisions, and that determination was tantamount to a finding of invalidity. Section 84-A, added in 1956, operates prospectively: it bars a declaration or finding of invalidity after it came into force but does not affect an adjudication in which invalidity had already been found. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: old_transfer and prior_invalidity_finding and finding_final_before_later_validation_measure and later_validation_sought_for_same_transfer

predicates.old_transfer: The transfer was made before a later measure made transfers of that kind eligible for validation.
predicates.prior_invalidity_finding: An authority found the transfer invalid in proceedings concerning it.
predicates.finding_final_before_later_validation_me: The finding of invalidity became final before the later validation measure came into force.
predicates.later_validation_sought_for_same_transfe: A party later sought validation of the same transfer under the new measure.

issues.definition: When a transfer was found invalid and that finding became final before a later validation measure took effect, a later application concerning that transfer does not displace the final finding.

issues.legal_issue: A person with an interest in the matter may invoke the summary remedy for eviction even if that person is not the landlord.
material_facts: Villagers sought the summary eviction of the transferee, alleging that the transfer contravened restrictions on transfers of agricultural land.
The villagers were interested in the land because they sought its use for village grazing.
The transferee argued that the remedy could be invoked only by the landlord.
issues.conclusion: An application under section 84 need not be made by the landlord alone; any interested person may invoke the remedy.
issues.legal_principle: Section 84 of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 permits any person interested to resort to its remedy. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.summary_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding seeks summary eviction of a person alleged to be in possession under an invalid transfer.
predicates.applicant_has_interest_in_the_matter: The applicant has an interest in the land or in the relief sought.

issues.definition: An interested applicant in a summary eviction proceeding may seek that remedy without being the landlord.

issues.legal_issue: In a summary eviction proceeding based on an allegedly invalid transfer, the Collector must determine whether the person sought to be evicted is in possession under that transfer.
material_facts: The villagers sought summary eviction on the ground that the transferee possessed the land under a transfer alleged to contravene statutory restrictions.
The Collector considered the transfer's validity in deciding the relief sought, including relief concerning land proposed to be set aside for grazing.
issues.conclusion: When the section 84 remedy is invoked, it is the Collector's duty to decide whether the person sought to be evicted is in possession pursuant to an invalid transfer.
issues.legal_principle: Section 84, including clause (a), requires the Collector to decide whether the person sought to be evicted is in possession pursuant to an invalid transfer. The Collector's finding on whether the transfer contravenes sections 63 or 64 is tantamount to a finding that the transfer is invalid; the Act does not provide for a separate formal declaration by a revenue authority. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.summary_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding seeks summary eviction of a person from land.
predicates.possession_claimed_under_allegedly_inval: The person sought to be evicted is alleged to possess the land under a transfer said to be invalid.

issues.definition: In a summary eviction proceeding, when possession is alleged to rest on an invalid transfer, the Collector must determine whether it does.
